title: candidate deep dive - runtime notes (Noa Sahin)
body:
Context / quick summary:
- Interview loop today: 90m deep-dive with candidate Noa Sahin (senior infra/runtime). Came in strong on low-level memory/KV-cache tradeoffs.
- Role fit: leaning infra/runtime engineer (latency focused) — possible match for runtime-core team.
- Mood: calm, thoughtful, sometimes verbose. Defers when uncertain. Good communicator.

High level impression:
- Knows the latency tradeoffs end-to-end: batching, pipeline stalls, kernel choices. Used concrete examples from past product (edge LLM inference at startup).
- Strong intuition for where tail latency shows up (scheduler jitter, PCIe stalls, torch stream sync).
- Less confident on distributed rollout policy design and multi-tenant quota enforcement — conceptual answers but light on concrete implementation details.

Technical deep-dive notes (freeform):
- KV cache: described two-tier approach in previous system: hot-slot in GPU LRU + warm-tier in host RAM with async prefetch to GPU. Emphasized avoiding GPU memcpy on critical path via pinned buffers.
- Prefetch policy: heuristic based on request-origin token entropy + recent prefix reuse. Mentioned using bloom filters to avoid unnecessary fetches.
- Batching: advocated adaptive batching with a small micro-batch fast-path for sub-10ms requests (single-token continuation) and larger batching for throughput windows. Sketch: maintain two queues, fast-path with pre-warmed contexts.
- Quantization: prefers 8-bit dynamic per-layer quantize with selective FP16 for attention score stability. Had a simple benchmark claim: 2-4% perplexity increase vs float32 but 2.5x throughput. Wanted to re-run on our Llama+variants.
- Kernel tuning: comfortable reading kernel traces, suggested a tool-chain: perf / nvprof (or Nsight) + custom microbench harness for token-latency 95/99 analysis.
- Failure modes: highlighted cache coherence bugs when migrating contexts across GPUs — gave an example where stale KV pointers caused OOM after live-migration.

System-design / product-context thoughts:
- When asked about cold start for cached contexts across regions, proposed probabilistic prewarming by observing country-level traffic patterns and keeping small LRU warm in every region. Notes on cost: prewarm budget must be per-customer SLA (good tie to Dedicated offering).
- Routing policy: suggested weight-based routing combining latency SLO, cost-per-token, and model-quality tier; fallback to smaller quantized variant on capacity pressure.

Red flags / risks:
- Limited experience with large-scale rollout automation (A/B rollouts, canary analysis). Has theory but fewer shipping stories here.
- Security/compliance context: glossed over KMS/HSM details when probed — likely needs pairing with security engineer for Private deployments.
- Prefers kernel-level optimizations vs productized orchestration — potential culture fit question for teams that do more ops/product.

Strengths / differentiators:
- Excellent low-level debug skills (kernel traces / NVTX example he walked through).
- Practical pragmatism: tradeoffs are framed in cost-latency terms; often gave small experiments to validate assumptions.
- Good domain knowledge for inference engine internals (KV layout, pinned buffers, streams).

Suggested follow-ups / pairing tasks:
- Small pairing: repro a jitter case on local harness. Task: given microbench harness (link in GH PR), reproduce 99th percentile spike introduced by host->device memcpy in concurrent streams. Timebox: 3 hours pairing + 30m debrief.
- Take-home (optional): design doc (2 pages) for multi-tenant cache eviction + prefetch policy tradeoffs. Include cost model and simple rollout plan. 48h turnaround.

Suggested interview score / recommendation (draft):
- Technical: strong (7/10) — deep infra chops, kernel-level confidence.
- System design / rollout: moderate (5.5/10) — conceptual but limited shipping examples.
- Communication / collaboration: strong (8/10).
- Overall: recommend for onsite/next-stage pairing with runtime engineers; consider for Senior Engineer on runtime-core with mentorship on rollouts & compliance.

Open questions to resolve in follow-up:
- Exact scale: how many GPUs / contexts has she operated concurrently in production? (asked, got approximate "hundreds" but need concrete numbers)
- Experience with multi-tenant accounting and quota enforcement in a high-throughput environment — examples?
- Familiarity with KMS/HSM and audit logging for Private deployments — any hands-on?

Notes / miscellaneous snippets captured during interview:
- "We used pinned staging buffers so memcpy didn't block the main CUDA stream — that saved us 6-8ms p50 per call."
- Mentions an incident post-live-migration where stale device pointers caused cascading OOMs; says they added a pointer-scan step in the handoff path.
- References: pointed to an internal repo (will request link) and a PR he authored that optimized attention kernel launch parameters.

Action items for hiring team:
- Marcus: schedule 3-hour pairing session (kernel repro) — suggest Tue morning next week.
- Elena: follow up on ask for concrete production scale numbers + any public links to PRs.
- Noa (owner): prep short 1-page design for cache eviction if moving forward.

Personal rating / gut check (quick):
- Fit for low-level runtime work: high.
- Fit for product/PLG-facing work (console/rollouts): medium-low.

End of scratchpad. Will tidy if moving candidate forward.
